item.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
item.description:
How many Fantastic Four movies is that, just since 200? Four?

I think I’ve actually seen them all. One even had a sequel And I’m not sure I can remember anything from any of them really.

This one has a nice cast, a fun, well done retro-futuristic aesthetic, found family, and some future/world building potential. It’s not the best MCU movie by any standard, but I think it might just be the best Fantastic Four film.

item.title: Thunderbolts*
item.description:
Yelena Belova: There’s something wrong with me. An emptiness. I thought it started when my sister died, but now it feels like something bigger. Just a void. Or maybe I’m just bored.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe has been a little rough for a while. A few good movies, but mostly, everything mostly feels by the book.

Thunderbolts*… is a surprisingly good movie.

It could have been forgettable. More action movie/big skybeam showdown/forgettable mirror villains. It could have been Marvel’s answer to The Suicide Squad (either really).

item.title: KPop Demon Hunters
item.description:
Better sit down for the show ‘cause I’m gonna show you How it’s done, done, done

Well that was a delightful surprise.

I’ve of course heard of KPop Demon Hunters, but I hadn’t really paid that much attention to it.

And then one of the songs was suggested to me on YouTube.

And another.

And they got stuck in my head.

Rumi: It is annoyingly catchy, though.

And then I finally watched it.

item.title: Captain America: Brave New World
item.description:
President Thaddeus Ross: When a Celestial mass emerged in the Indian Ocean, we did what we often do. We squabbled over it. Countries rushed in to claim it as their own, setting up research facilities to exploit its resources. What was found inside that island is nothing short of the discovery of the millennium. Its potential applications in tech, in medicine, in defense are immeasurable. It’s even more indestructible than vibranium. And it’s not controlled by an isolationist nation. Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you adamantium.

So. We’re going to not only finally deal with that mess from Eternals, but we’re also going to finally get in universe adamantium? Interesting strategy.

In any case, we have a new Captain America. I wasn’t sure Anthony Mackie could head a movie in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (or S2 of Altered Carbon for that matter), but I actually quite enjoyed him this time around. I think Danny Ramirez / Joaquin Torres / the new Falcon really helped with that.

Otherwise, we have Harrison Ford taking over for William Hurt as Ross. I’m… still surprised when I see Harrison Ford still being quite as active an actor as he is. It was already slightly odd in Kindom of the Crystal Skull… and that was more than 15 years ago.

Overall, a step up from the recent spate of Marvel movies/TV. Hnoestly, it’s been probably since Spider-Man: No Way Home or Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness… Still, a decent action flick?

Onward!
